# Scene editor E5: the hub receives, shows, accepts and checks scene edits

Step 5 of 6 of the in-game scene editor. Design page: https://claude.ai/artifact/GZf1vP9iD5ChT2cx2BGD6p. Read PROJECT-BRIEF.md first, then Grep context.md for "Mikkadr Hub P4" and "Mikkadr Hub P5" and read only the security notes there. Needs E1 to E4. No model call anywhere in this step's code.

## Goal
"Send to hub" in the editor files a scene edit in the hub. The hub shows it under Waiting for you with a before and after picture. Accept writes `dist/scene-edits.js`. "Apply to game" in the editor does send and accept in one press. A Check button runs the release and the tests as a plain script.

## Build
1. `hub/scene.js` (pure) and `hub/scene-store.mjs`: a scene edit is `{id, at, status: waiting|accepted|denied|superseded, edits, summary, base, check}` kept in `.hub/scene/<id>.json` (temp file then rename). `base` is the hash of `dist/scene-edits.js` the edit was made on.
2. Route `POST /api/scene/propose` in `hub/server.js`: the ONE write route that accepts a foreign origin, and only `http://localhost:8000` and `http://127.0.0.1:8000` (the dev game). Answer the CORS preflight for this route only and for those origins only. Still required: Host check, `Content-Type: application/json`, 64 KB cap. The body is re-validated on the hub with `normaliseEdits` and `validateEdits` from `dist/scene-edit.js` against the real prop list, the scene keys and `MAP.playable`; anything invalid is refused with the reasons. The page never sends a path, and nothing from the body reaches a file name or a shell.
3. Route `GET /api/scene/current` for the same two origins: the accepted overlay's hash, so the editor can tell when its base is stale.
4. Hub page: Waiting for you gets "Scene edit: 3 added, 2 moved, 1 removed" (`hub/waiting.js`), opening a Scene page with a top-down SVG of the affected area before and after (footprints from prop sizes, added green, moved with an arrow, removed struck out), the list of changes, and Accept, Deny (with a note) and Check. A new edit supersedes an older waiting one.
5. Accept (same-origin POST with the hub token, as the run routes do): refuse with 409 when `base` no longer matches the file; otherwise write `dist/scene-edits.js` from `normaliseEdits` output with a fixed serialiser (stable key order, no BOM, the header comment kept), keep the previous file content in the record so "Undo this accept" can restore it, and mark the item "needs check".
6. `POST /api/scene/apply` for the two game origins: propose and accept in one call, for the editor's "Apply to game" button. It must pass the same validation and the same 409 rule. It carries a one-time token the editor first fetches from `GET /api/scene/token` (same two origins), so a stray page cannot apply an edit blind.
7. Check: runs `npm run release -- --force` then `npm test` as child processes (no model, no shell string built from input), under the shared `.hub/run.lock`, low priority, with pass or fail and the failing test names stored on the record. Refused while a run or a chat turn is active.
8. Editor (`dist/scene-editor.js`): enable "Send to hub" and "Apply to game"; show "The hub is not running (npm run hub)" when it cannot be reached and keep the edit in the browser; after an apply, show "Applied: restart the game to load it from disk" and keep the live view as it is.
9. Tests: `tests/hub-scene.mjs` (store, supersede, 409 on stale base, serialiser output is stable and parses back equal, undo restores) and server tests: a foreign origin other than the two is refused, preflight only on these routes, oversized and invalid bodies refused with reasons, accept needs the hub token, apply needs the one-time token, Check refused while busy. Add a Scene screenshot to `scripts/hub-shots.mjs`.

## Rules
- The hub never commits or pushes. The only game file it may write is `dist/scene-edits.js`.
- Do not loosen any existing route: the new origin rule applies to the three scene routes named above and nothing else.
- No BOM. After the change run `npm run release -- --force`, then `npm test`. Stop with tests passing; report failures honestly, and list what was not seen in a real browser. If a test fails only because PROJECT-INDEX.md is stale, say so and do not edit generated files.
- Do not commit.

## Done when
An edit sent from the game appears in the hub, Accept writes the overlay file, Check reports pass or fail, Apply to game does it in one press, and every refused case above has a test.
